en.name: Peter Canisius
en.summary: Dutch Jesuit and Doctor of the Church whose catechisms and preaching are credited with preserving Catholicism across much of Germany during the Reformation.
en.body: Peter Canisius joined the newly founded Society of Jesus and became one of its most effective figures in Central Europe during the turbulent decades of the Protestant Reformation, when large parts of Germany, Austria, and Switzerland appeared on the verge of turning entirely Protestant. He wrote a catechism that went through hundreds of editions and translations and became the primary tool for reintroducing systematic Catholic instruction to confused and religiously divided populations, while also founding and reforming Jesuit colleges across the German-speaking lands to train a new generation of well-formed clergy. His tireless preaching, writing, and diplomatic mediation between conflicting factions are widely credited by historians with holding a substantial Catholic population in Central Europe together during a period when it might easily have been lost entirely. He died in 1597 and was canonized and declared a Doctor of the Church simultaneously in 1925.
